title: Seller Propensity Matrix Playbook - annotated draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft: a compact seller-facing playbook that maps buyer signals to a recommended engagement lane (propensity lanes). Goal = help AEs and SEs pick the highest-leverage play (pilot, quick PoC, reserved capacity conversation, or executive-led procurement) in under 10 minutes.

Audience:
- Field sellers (SEs, AEs) running discovery and technical pilots
- SDRs prepping for technical handoffs
- CS for early pilot success guidance

One-line thesis:
If we translate observable signals into deterministic play lanes, sellers spend less time guessing and more time closing with the right evidence and configuration.

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Run the qualification checklist (first table).
2) Compute a raw propensity score (sum of weighted signals).
3) Pick the recommended lane and follow the play checklist and battlecard snippets.
4) Log outcome in JIRA/Playbook tracker.

Propensity signals (candidate list, with weights) - quick reference:
- Data sensitivity: low/medium/high (weights: 0/2/4)
- Latency SLO requirement: <200ms / 200-600ms / >600ms (weights 3/1/0)
- Estimated RPS: <5 / 5-100 / >100 (weights 0/2/4)
- Budget/decision owner: product/eng (low) vs finance/procurement (high) (weights 0/3)
- Existing infra preference: cloud hosted / hybrid / on prem (weights 0/2/4)
- Integration timeline: <2 weeks / 2-8 weeks / >8 weeks (weights 3/1/0)
- Model fidelity bar (human-in-loop required?): yes/no (weights 2/0)

Scoring quick math: add weights, normalize to 0-20. Lane mapping (draft):
- 0-6: Quick Win lane - lightweight hosted API + standard prompts, aim to convert in 1-2 weeks.
- 7-12: Pilot lane - technical PoC, focus on embeddings/semantic search + caching; include SLA-lite benchmarks.
- 13-16: Dedicated lane - reserved capacity conversation, include perf/cost modeling and migration plan.
- 17-20: Private lane - early legal/procurement engagement, KMS/HSM and on-prem checklist.

Play lanes - what to do (checklists + snippets)
1) Quick Win lane (score 0-6) - 1 slide summary for seller:
- Lead with demos: 30s latency evidence, 2 token-cost bullets
- Starter offer: free trial credits + templated example app (support email + onboarding snippet)
- Fast success metrics: time-to-first-successful-call, accuracy on sample prompt set
- Common pushback and micro-responses: "Can we host ourselves?" -> "Yes, later - we can export models + infra plan on pilot"

2) Pilot lane (7-12) - seller brief:
- Request minimal dataset + two representative prompts
- Offer staging environment with per-route dashboards (show cost/latency graphs)
- Trial configuration: prefix caching + aggressive batching for cost control
- Success criteria template: latency < 400ms P95, token cost < $0.007 per 1k tokens, 3 production-like scenarios validated
- Evidence to bring: perf trace screenshots, sample roll-forward plan, fallback policy snippet

3) Dedicated lane (13-16) - negotiation cues:
- Bring capacity math: RPS * tokens * commit months -> estimate $/month; prepare two pricing bands (conservative/optimistic)
- Migration hooks: export/import KV cache, model pinning recommendations
- SLA expectations: uptime targets and penalty language (link to draft contract clauses)
- Stakeholders: SRE, infra procurement, legal (engagement play: call with infra architect + capacity deep dive)

4) Private lane (17-20) - enterprise play:
- Start with compliance questionnaire, KMS/HSM details, VPC peering checklist
- Offer on-prem packaging options & uplift services (PS days estimate)
- Provide a security pack (audit log sampling, retention windows) and initial runbook for incident response
- Engage account exec + solutions engineering + security org early

Battlecard snippets (short, usable lines sellers can copy):
- Competitor: Large public LLM clouds (pricing/latency objections):
  - "Why Redwood?" -> "We map the same model surface to a lower operational token cost via batching + prefix cache; customers typically see 20-40% cost reduction in early pilots - we can model your workload live."
  - Tech rebuttal: "If you need predictable throughput, our Dedicated pool guarantees capacity and autoscaling with priority lanes for critical routes."
- Competitor: Pure self-hosted inference vendors:
  - Objection: "We want to avoid vendor lock-in" -> "We support identical rollout policies and model pinning; you can export snapshots and run a private deployment when ready - many teams start hosted and migrate on their timeline."
- Competitor: Specialized embeddings providers:
  - Talk track: "Our unified API gives you embeddings + generation + reranking; engineering one integration reduces maintenance and gives consistent cost/latency controls."

Top seller scripts (30s / 90s):
- 30s (engineering): "We give you a consistent API for embeddings and chat, plus observability per-request. If you share two sample prompts and traffic profile, we'll run a quick performance model and show expected token economics in 48 hours."
- 90s (procurement): "We offer hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options with clear capacity math and contract levels. For pilots, we recommend a short reserved capacity pilot so we can validate throughput at scale while you retain the option to go private later."

Objection handling (cheat snippets):
- "We don't trust external APIs with sensitive PII." -> "We offer private deployments + KMS integration and an on-prem package; for hosted pilots we can sign a DPA and narrow data flows during POC."
- "Latency is the blocker." -> "We'll run a quick perf trace on your prompts; often fixed overheads are due to pipeline choices and can be reduced with batching/pinning and model quantization - we can show P95 improvements in the first week."

Pilot playbook - minimal artifacts to run (seller checklist):
- Signed pilot SOW (template link: confluence:pilot-sow-template)
- Sample prompts + representative dataset (anonymized)
- Traffic profile + expected concurrency windows
- Access for SE to logs/traces + one contact on infra team
- Success metrics pre-agreed and internal watchlist (latency, token cost, accuracy/regression on eval set)

KPIs & signals to log during pilot (quick):
- Latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, batch size distribution, failed requests/day, model drift alerts matched to eval prompts

Small annex: quick evaluation prompt set (starter pack) - copy-paste:
- Retrieval QA scenario: "Given customer billing history and subscription notes, summarize top 3 churn risks and an action suggestion."
- Conversational assistant: "User: I need to refund an incorrect charge. System: walk me through the steps and list verification signals."
- Classification: "Classify incoming text into urgency: low/medium/high with a 1-2 sentence justification."

Open questions & TODOs (team action items):
- [ ] Finalize weighting scheme with RM (data-driven weights rather than hand-tuned). Assigned: Marcus. Due: 2026-03-12.
- [ ] Build a one-click scoring sheet (Google Sheet) for sellers to drop signals and get lane. Owner: Sofia. Blockers: sample distribution for weights.
- [ ] Assemble a short demo repo showing "Quick Win" integration (starter Node + Python examples). Owner: DevX.
- [ ] Validate pricing examples with finance for Dedicated lane ranges. Owner: Diego.

Notes / rough rationale (freeform):
- Why a matrix instead of just heuristics: sellers want determinism; a small score reduces back-and-forth with prospects and standardizes internal handoffs (SE -> CS -> Finance).
- Keep the Quick Win lane intentionally easy: conversion velocity matters more than perfect ROI modeling at discovery.
- Pilot lane should default to enabling cache/batching because most cost objections evaporate with a conservative config.

Appendix: live links (placeholders)
- example perf dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/pilot-template (internal)
- pilot SOW template: confluence:pilot-sow-template
- quick play repo: github:org/inference-quick-win-starter

Slack shorthand to use when sharing this doc to #se-playbooks:
"Draft: Propensity matrix playbook - distilled lanes for sellers. Please comment on weights + lane thresholds. Key ask: Marcus to run weight sims on historical pilots."
